correctness.rationale: Every anonymous four-candidate profile with 1..5 complete strict ballots lies in a weak composition over 24 ranking types (counts 24,300,2600,17550,98280). Reconstructed a separate multiplicity-based recursion branching over ALL tied Baldwin minima, with Nanson removing all strictly sub-average candidates and keeping equal-score stalling nonunique. It finds no different unique outcomes for n<=4; at n=5 exactly 384 anonymous, weighted 24480 labeled, out of 7,232,544 labeled cases unique for both; canonicalizing under all 24 candidate relabelings yields 16 orbits all size 24. Confirmed witness 2 BDCA +1 CABD +2 DCAB elects B under Baldwin and D under Nanson by explicit score recount. Exhaustive finite search is legitimate because the stated domain is finite, but proves nothing beyond n<=5 and specified tie convention.

evidence: Narodytska-Walsh-Xia explicitly define simultaneous removal of all below-mean Borda candidates for Nanson and removal of one lowest candidate for Baldwin.

value.rationale: The smallest electorate for guaranteed different unique Nanson and Baldwin outcomes is a natural comparison of two historically connected elimination rules. Exact unconditional and conditional incidences plus the complete first symmetry layer are independently useful, beyond one example and beyond finite software reproducibility alone. The result is bounded to four candidates, strict ballots and explicitly defined tie independence.

final_claim: Among complete strict four-candidate profiles with n<=5, Nanson strict-below-average and tie-independent Baldwin have distinct unique winners first at n=5; exactly 384 anonymous and 24480 labeled conflicts, in sixteen size-24 candidate orbits.
limitations: Tie independence is defined by all legal Baldwin eliminations and unforced Nanson stalling; external tie-breakers change the event.
Complete finite enumeration applies only to four candidates, n<=5; existence of older unindexed census remains a risk.
